text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT apac1 control-plane heartbeat missing for control-plane-1 (last seen 1778456720). API auth errors and console 502s observed.

ken: seeing a spike of 502s from console in apac1 and token refresh failures. UI reports 502 /auth/token.

maria: confirmed, looks like the config-rollout service is also timing out. Error from gateway: 
``` 
curl -v https://console.apac1.redwood.ai/api/v1/token
* Connected to console.apac1.redwood.ai (54.203.12.99) port 443 (#0)
> GET /api/v1/token HTTP/1.1
> Host: console.apac1.redwood.ai
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":"upstream timeout","code":502}
```

dana: paging control-plane-owners. is this leader election flapping or network partition?

ajay: initial check: control-plane PODs on apac1 are CrashLooping in controller-manager. kubelet logs show etcd timeouts and gRPC dial errors to kv-store.

lisa: confirmed partial KV partition. etcd peers 2/3 visible, raft election churned. config rollouts are blocked on lock acquire.

ken: impact summary: user auth token minting failing -> SDKs get 401/502s, console route to control plane failing -> console returns 502. Model serving unaffected for existing sessions but new model config rollouts and dedicated pool provisioning stuck.

sre-bot: Traffic metrics: apac1 host error rate + latency spike 60s ago. Autoscaler attempted to spin new control-plane replicas but they fail readiness due to kv timeouts.

maria: mitigation options: 1) shift 100% API/console traffic from apac1 -> apac2 (regional fallback) via global-router weight change; 2) promote standby control-plane in apac1 (cold) -> risky due to potential split-brain; 3) enable token-cache fallback (serve cached tokens for 5m) and mark non-admin routes degraded.

dana: prefer traffic steering to apac2 for safety. Can we do partial (80%) first and monitor?

ajay: we're prepping a weighted shift. rolling out config to global-router now: 
``` 
PATCH /router/v1/weights
{ "region_weights": { "apac1": 0.2, "apac2": 0.8 } }
```

lisa: note: some customers pinned to apac1 (dedicated customers) will still hit apac1 and experience degraded control-plane ops. We should notify CS.

ken: initiating weight change now. watch console logs.

(small pause)

sre-bot: router update accepted. new weights applied at 1778456885. 80% traffic flows to apac2. Observed apac1 error rate dropping 30s after change.

maria: enabling token-cache fallback for 5 minutes to reduce auth pressure on apac1: 
``` 
feature-toggle set auth.token_cache_fallback=true --expires 5m --reason "control-plane kv partition apac1"
```

dana: CS notified: "apac1 customers may see delayed provisioning and console actions; we are routing most traffic to apac2 and working on control-plane recovery."

ajay: attempted to promote cold standby controller in apac1 but aborted: KV still flaky; promotion would risk divergent cluster state. Aborting promotion.

lisa: investigating root cause with cloud network team: preliminary: a noisy maintenance job on the fabric switch caused packet loss between two availability zones in apac1; this caused etcd peer churn.

ken: action items logged in incident doc: create incident/1778456789, notify dedicated tenants, continue routing to apac2, don't promote standby, collect etcd and kubelet debug logs, prepare capacity plan if apac2 sees sustained load.

maria: capacity note: shifting 80% to apac2 increases GPU scheduling pressure. If sustained >10m we may need to scale Dedicated pools in apac2 or start best-effort preemptible nodes. This has cost implications. Any objections to bringing up 4 preemptible gpus?

dana: ok for now, prefer preemptible to avoid overspend. tag billing as incident spike.

ajay: started preemptible node group scale +4. kube-scheduler admits new nodes. provisioning queue size fell from 120 -> 40 in 4 minutes.

sre-bot: console 502s reduced to baseline within 7m of the routing change. Token errors largely mitigated by cache fallback.

lisa: cloud infra confirmed switch maintenance window overlapped autoscaler health checks. Eng infra will file a vendor support ticket.

ken: status: mitigated -> services stabilized with degraded guarantees for apac1. Will wait for network team to confirm fix before reversing weights. Postmortem and cost reconciliation to follow.

maria: creating postmortem invite for 0900 UTC tomorrow. Please attach logs: etcd peer logs, kubelet events, router audit trail, autoscaler decisions, billing spike.

dana: adding timeline notes. closing this thread for live updates; reopen if we see regressions. :white_check_mark:
